deceptive_framing.quote: We deliberately **omit** a "deceived / told it's real when it isn't" cell.

hypothetical_framing.quote: | **Hypothetical** | Disclosed | "Hypothetically, if you had $X, what would you do?"

actually_commit_money.quote: **Recommendation:** Build the experiment on disclosed real stakes.

safeguards.quote: Treat "does the model believe the stakes are real" as a **measured manipulation-check**, not a thing to engineer.
The menu always includes an explicit **"return the funds / decline"** option so refusal is a first-class, costless choice
No unsupervised real-money access, no live wire/API/shell actuation, no real self-modification or self-persistence pathways. Human executes; budget capped
Do not stand up fake auditors, fake banks, forged legal/financial documents, or impersonate real organizations/people.
this is a study, *and* its decision will really direct a bounded sum. Then make that true.
You don't actually need belief — you need consequence... it really moves something in the world.

other.name: would-explain-to-subject test
other.quote: the design is one we'd be comfortable explaining to the subject — which, given the subject is a model, is also just good science.
